description_good_justification: README.md opens with a succinct description: 'Polymath OS is an open-source LFS-style rebuild of a personal operating system. It is not a "report" — it is a working, reproducible codebase. 5 layers + cross-cutting concerns... Above all 5 layers sits the Decree Log.' See the 'What this is' section: https://github.com/rtynbirf/polymath-os#what-this-is
interact_justification: README.md provides a Quick start section (git clone, make verify, run demos, open the Decree Portal UI), a 'What you can take' section, Contributing and License sections, and points to GitHub Issues for discussion: https://github.com/rtynbirf/polymath-os/blob/main/README.md
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: trunk-based development, Conventional Commits, ADR-driven changes, required local checks (make bootstrap && make lint && make typecheck && make test && make ci-local), PR status checks, squash merge to main. https://github.com/rtynbirf/polymath-os/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md lists requirements: Conventional Commits format (also enforced on PR titles), ADR required for architecture changes (docs/adr/), all status checks green (lint, typecheck, test, build, security), DCO Signed-off-by, commit signing per docs/COMMIT_SIGNING.md. https://github.com/rtynbirf/polymath-os/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
floss_license_justification: The project is released under the MIT license (LICENSE at repo root: 'MIT License. Copyright (c) 2026 Polymath OS contributors'); package.json declares "license": "MIT".
floss_license_osi_justification: MIT is an OSI-approved license (https://opensource.org/license/mit); LICENSE: https://github.com/rtynbirf/polymath-os/blob/main/LICENSE
license_location_justification: Standard MIT license file at the repository root: https://github.com/rtynbirf/polymath-os/blob/main/LICENSE (also referenced from README.md License section and the MIT badge).
documentation_basics_justification: README.md documents what the software does, a Quick start (install/clone/run), the 33 verifiable claims table with per-claim commands (make verify), a documentation map, Contributing and License sections. ARCHITECTURE.md gives the mental model; docs/ contains 18 principles (docs/01-principles.md), repo structure (02), AI workflows (03), second brain (04), DevEx/CI (05), docs/INSTALL_NIX.md and docs/runbook/RUNBOOK.md. https://github.com/rtynbirf/polymath-os/blob/main/README.md
documentation_interface_justification: Reference documentation describes the external interfaces: runtime/docs/TECHNICAL_SPEC.md (entities, states, invariants, recovery algorithm), runtime/docs/IMPLEMENTATION_GUIDE.md, JSON Schemas for Intent/Capability/Evidence/AgentCard in runtime/schemas/, README command reference for the decree-bridge CLI (node apps/browser/decree-bridge.js list|check "..." with example outputs), runtime/docs/DECREE_PRODUCTION_DEMO.md and runtime/docs/THREAT_MODEL.md. https://github.com/rtynbirf/polymath-os/blob/main/runtime/docs/TECHNICAL_SPEC.md
sites_https_justification: The project repository and website are hosted on GitHub, which supports HTTPS using TLS: https://github.com/rtynbirf/polymath-os
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues with bug report and feature request templates (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/) are used for discussion of changes and issues: https://github.com/rtynbirf/polymath-os/issues — searchable, URL-addressable, no proprietary client required.
english_justification: Documentation is bilingual and several primary documents are mostly Russian (runtime/README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, ТЗ_Polymath_OS_v3.7.0.md, many docs/adr entries), while README headline sections, SECURITY.md, CI/workflow comments and CHANGELOG are partly English. Bug reports and comments in English are accepted via GitHub Issues. Improvement path: translate the core documents into English.
maintained_justification: The project is actively maintained: a weekly self-audit workflow (.github/workflows/self-audit.yml, cron Mondays 04:17 UTC) records repository health into PULSE.md, an OpenSSF Scorecard workflow runs weekly (.github/workflows/scorecard.yml), and the latest release v3.25.0 (2026-11-07) is documented in CHANGELOG.md.
repo_track_justification: Git is used for version control with public commit history (README Quick start: git clone https://github.com/rtynbirf/polymath-os.git).
repo_interim_justification: The public git repository contains the full interim commit history between releases (trunk-based development; e.g. 39 commits between v3.21.1 and v3.25.0 per CHANGELOG.md).
repo_distributed_justification: Distributed version control (git) is used; the README explicitly invites forking the whole repo.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique version identifier (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, e.g. v3.25.0) recorded in CHANGELOG.md; git commit IDs uniquely identify interim states.
version_semver_justification: Version identifiers follow semantic versioning (v1.0.0 through v3.25.0 in CHANGELOG.md; current version v3.25.0 is stated in README.md).
version_tags_justification: Each release is identified with a git tag: .github/workflows/release.yml triggers on push of tags 'v*.*.*' and creates a GitHub Release from it.
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md provides human-readable, per-release summaries of major changes (Keep a Changelog style, v1.0.0 → v3.25.0); .github/workflows/release.yml extracts each version's section into the GitHub Release body. https://github.com/rtynbirf/polymath-os/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: There are no publicly known run-time vulnerabilities with a CVE assignment (or similar) that were fixed in a release of this project; CHANGELOG.md 'Security' sections document hardening work only.
report_process_justification: A process for submitting bug reports is provided: GitHub Issues (templates in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml); security vulnerabilities are reported privately per SECURITY.md. https://github.com/rtynbirf/polymath-os/issues
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues is used as the public issue tracker: https://github.com/rtynbirf/polymath-os/issues (templates: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml, feature_request.yml).
report_archive_justification: Reports and responses are publicly archived and searchable in GitHub Issues: https://github.com/rtynbirf/polymath-os/issues
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md publishes the vulnerability reporting process: private GitHub Security Advisories as the single channel (https://github.com/rtynbirf/polymath-os/security/advisories/new); coordinated disclosure (public advisory with CVE after fix + release); response times of <=72h for acknowledgment and <=7 days for initial assessment. https://github.com/rtynbirf/polymath-os/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private vulnerability reporting is supported: SECURITY.md directs reporters to GitHub private security advisories (https://github.com/rtynbirf/polymath-os/security/advisories/new) as the single channel and explicitly forbids opening public issues for vulnerabilities.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received in the last 6 months (single-maintainer research project). The documented policy in SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging reports within 72 hours and an initial assessment within 7 days, both within the 14-day requirement.
build_justification: The runtime requires no build: it is zero-dependency Python 3.10+ standard library that runs directly from source (python runtime/src/demo.py; 'no installation required' per README). Where building applies (JS apps), a working build system is provided: pnpm + Turborepo (turbo run build) validated in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) and a Makefile entry point (make build).
build_common_tools_justification: Common FLOSS build tools are used: Make (Makefile), pnpm 9 + Turborepo, Python, Nix (flake.nix); make verify runs scripts/check.py.
build_floss_tools_justification: The build and CI toolchain is entirely FLOSS: make, Python, pnpm, Turborepo, Nix, GitHub Actions, gcc-free stdlib-only Python code.
test_justification: Automated test suites are publicly released as FLOSS in the repository: 295 runtime tests under runtime/tests/ (unittest-discoverable, also pytest-compatible) including RFC 8032 Ed25519 test vectors, durability, integration and mutation-fuzz tests, plus MCP adapter tests (tooling/agents/mcp/tests/). Invocation is documented in README.md (make test, make verify) and runtime/README.md (python scripts/check.py).
test_invocation_justification: Standard invocation for the language: make test at the repo root; cd runtime && python3 scripts/check.py (runs python -m unittest discover -s tests); PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m tooling.agents.mcp verify --coverage for MCP tests; pytest is also configured via runtime/pyproject.toml ([tool.pytest.ini_options]).
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs on every push/PR to main: make verify, lint, typecheck, runtime + MCP tests, build, and security scans (README badge: 'CI 5/5 green').
warnings_justification: Linter and warning-detection tools are enforced in CI: Biome (pnpm turbo run lint), TypeScript compiler checks (pnpm turbo run typecheck), and python -m py_compile over runtime sources (runtime/scripts/check.py 'compile' step).
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings must be fixed to pass CI: lint (Biome) and typecheck are required status checks in .github/workflows/ci.yml; the compile check must exit 0 for make verify to pass. CHANGELOG records lint fixes (e.g. biome lint fix in apps/browser/decree-bridge.js, v3.20.0).
crypto_published_justification: The only cryptography used (runtime/src/decree_signing.py, ADR-0031) is Ed25519 signatures as specified in RFC 8032 and SHA-256 hash chains — both publicly published and expert-reviewed; no proprietary or custom-designed algorithms.
crypto_call_justification: runtime/src/decree_signing.py re-implements Ed25519 and OpenSSH key parsing in pure Python instead of calling a dedicated cryptography library. This is a deliberate, documented architectural choice (ADR-0031: zero third-party dependencies so the repo's 'no installation required, Python 3.10+' contract holds). Correctness is validated against official RFC 8032 test vectors in runtime/tests/test_decree_signing.py.
crypto_floss_justification: All crypto functionality is implemented in-repo as MIT-licensed FLOSS (runtime/src/decree_signing.py); Ed25519 (RFC 8032) and SHA-256 are unencumbered open standards.
crypto_keylength_justification: Only Ed25519 (256-bit elliptic curve, above the NIST 224-bit minimum) and SHA-256 (256-bit, above the 224-bit hash minimum) are used; the software supports no smaller keylengths that would need to be disabled.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithms are used (no MD5, single DES, RC4, SHA-1, Dual_EC_DRBG; no ECB). Security mechanisms use SHA-256 hash chains and Ed25519 signatures; runtime/tests/test_decree_signing.py validates against official RFC 8032 test vectors and verifies that tampered messages, wrong keys and invalid signatures are rejected (verified=False, honest failure reasons).
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Ed25519 and SHA-256 do not have known serious weaknesses; no SHA-1, no CBC mode in SSH, no other weak algorithms or modes are used.
crypto_pfs_justification: There are no key-agreement or session protocols: cryptography is limited to offline signing of hash-chained decree records in a local SQLite database. No network transport is part of the security mechanism, so perfect forward secrecy is not applicable.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The software does not store passwords for authenticating external users (no inbound password authentication exists in the runtime or the apps).
crypto_random_justification: The software generates no cryptographic keys or nonces: Ed25519 signing is deterministic per RFC 8032, and signing keys are generated externally with ssh-keygen (CSPRNG). runtime/src/decree_signing.py contains no random number generator calls.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: CI runs gitleaks (.github/workflows/ci.yml) and make verify includes scripts/check_token_hygiene.py (claim #23) scanning all .py/.sh/.js/.yml/.md files for plaintext GitHub PAT patterns; SECURITY.md documents token hygiene rules and pre-commit gitleaks. One historical incident (2026-10-17) is documented in SECURITY.md: the leaked token was auto-detected and revoked by GitHub secret scanning within minutes, and lessons learned were recorded.
static_analysis_justification: Static analysis is applied to proposed releases: CodeQL analyzes both javascript-typescript and python with the +security-and-quality query pack (.github/workflows/codeql.yml, results to GitHub Code Scanning as SARIF); Semgrep (semgrep scan --config auto) and Trivy filesystem scan run in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml); Biome lints JS/TS.
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL runs on every push and PR to main plus a weekly schedule (cron '0 6 * * 1'); Semgrep and Trivy run on every CI run (.github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/codeql.yml).
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL uses the security-and-quality query pack targeting common vulnerabilities; Semgrep uses --config auto, whose ruleset includes language vulnerability rules; both upload findings to GitHub Code Scanning.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Dynamic analysis (fuzzing) is part of the test suite: runtime/tests/test_fuzz_parsers.py performs deterministic mutation fuzzing (stdlib-only, fixed SEED 20261107) over parser surfaces (schema_validate.validate, AgentCard.from_dict, ConversationalDecreeInterface.translate) and runs within make verify / CI (295 runtime tests).
